newsitem.title: POLAND: INTERVIEW - New Polish finmin to curb budget, prices.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - New Polish finmin to curb budget, prices.

text.p: Poland's new Finance Minister Marek Belka, due to replace Grzegorz Kolodko on Tuesday, said he wanted to continue a policy of macroeconomic consolidation, curbing inflation and controlling the budget gap.
Belka, 45, told Reuters in a telephone interview he also wanted to speed up implementation of major structural reforms such as the privatisation of banks and social security reform.

"My policy will be that of full and active continuation of a policy of macroeconomic consolidation, fighting inflation and controlling the budget," said Belka, an independent economist currently advising President Aleksander Kwasniewski.

"I would like to participate more actively in the speeding up of several structural reforms awaiting us," he said, adding he would pay special attention to bank privatisaton and the long-delayed overhaul of the social security system.
Belka said he would not cut inflation at any cost because such a policy would cause economic collapse. But he said curbing price growth was a necessary condition for sustaining economic growth.
"We could cut inflation down to one digit in a short time, but that would be at the cost of economic collapse," he said.

"But fast economic growth cannot be sustained with inflation at current levels," Belka said. "It has to be reduced for the growth to be permanent. Without single digit inflation, for instance, we can only talk about an increase in housing output."
Year-on-year inflation in 1996 fell to 18.5 percent from 21.6 percent in 1995, and the budget draft for this year forecasts a drop to 13 percent in December 1997.
Gross domestic product (GDP) rose six percent last year, down from seven-percent growth in 1995. The government has forecast GDP up 5.5 percent this year.
